sections.html: Peaceful schooling fish reaching 6-7 cm in length.

Four species of the peculiar lizard tetras (Iguanodectes) are imported from time to time: I. spilurus, I. adujai, I. geisleri and I. purusii. But altogether there are eight accepted species and because of the similarity of these fishes and their wide distribution it is not always certain that the classification of the imports is correct. There are clear differences between the four species: I. spilurus has no red longitudinal banding; I. adujai has a very long anal fin compared to the other species; I. geisleri and I. purusii have a tricolor longitudinal banding – red-gold-black from top to bottom.

Very nice three-banded lizard tetras were received from the Rio Purus in Brazil and are addressed as I. purusii; it is not excluded that it is a local form of I. geisleri, which is clearly different in color from the animals received earlier from Venezuela; this is indicated by the low number of anal fin rays.

Iguanodectes are extremely attractive, somewhat sensitive fish, which attract attention by their unusual body shape and swimming style. They are especially sensitive during transport and acclimation. Once well acclimated they do not cause any problems and please the owner for many years.

These peaceful schooling fish got the name "lizard tetra" from their tooth shape, which reminds of the tooth shape in certain iguanas. In a show aquarium, single males from time to time separate themselves from the shoal and defend a broad-leaved plant (Anubias) against other males; females are then intensively courted.
Males are slimmer and more colorful than females, otherwise there are no externally recognizable sex differences.
Nothing is known about a successful breeding. Possibly they are adhesive spawners.
